newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Claridge CEO backs off bankruptcy talk.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Claridge CEO backs off bankruptcy talk.

text.p: The Claridge Hotel & Casino Corp no longer plans to seek a prepackaged bankruptcy plan in its negotiations with possible acquirer Hilton Hotels Corp, Claridge President and Chief Executive Robert Renneisen, said on Tuesday.
Renneisen told Reuters better than expected cash flows in 1997 have given the company better footing in negotiations with Hilton. Negotiations continue on cordial terms, he said.

"Hilton has expressed a strategic desire to acquire the Claridge and its going to take more negotiating time to reach what we believe to be fair value for the company," Renneisen said, adding that he prefers to do so "outside the shadow of bankruptcy."

Claridge on Tuesday said the improved cash flows made it possible to make the $5 million interest payment due March 5 on its 11-3/4 percent mortgage notes due 2002. The company in had indicated it expected to default on the payment.

At the same time, Claridge said it had reached an agreement with an unofficial noteholders committee to jointly move to dismiss an involuntary bankruptcy petition and a related state lawsuit. The lawsuit was filed by noteholders in an effort to garner full redemption value of the debt after it was learned a default was in the offing.

Claridge had discussed a prepackaged bankruptcy plan with Hilton in January. Under that proposal, Hilton would have acquired all the stock in Claridge in exchange for Hilton funding a cash distribution to noteholders.
Marc Grossman, senior vice president of corporate affairs at Hilton, said the company was in the process of evaluating Claridge's announcement of Tuesday and had no further comment.
Financial recovery for Claridge was, in part, due to good weather in January and February and the recent addition of a self-parking garage, Renneisen said.
The CEO said Claridge is current on all other financial obligations.
First quarter results will be available in May, he said.
